newsitem.title: POLAND: Poland to be ready to clear derivatives trade Feb.
newsitem.headline: Poland to be ready to clear derivatives trade Feb.

text.p: The Polish National Securities Depository (KDPW) is likely to be ready to clear derivatives transactions in February next year, deputy president of KDPW said on Wednesday.
Ludwik Sobolewski told Reuters a clearing house needed for the transactions was likely to be established in the next few weeks but the KDPW needed some time to set up a computer system.
"We want to be ready to clear the transactions in derivatives in February next year," he said.

The Warsaw Stock Exchange earlier said it could start derivatives trading in the second half of 1997 and it was likely to begin with derivatives on the WIG-20 share index, interest rates and the dollar/zloty and mark/zloty rates.
Sobolewski said the Warsaw Commodities Exchange and an organization grouping 16 banks System Pozagieldowego Obrotu Instrumentami Finansowymi (SPOIF) also planned to introduce derivatives.
He said, however, it was not yet decided whether they would use the KDPW's clearing house or set up their own houses.
